Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## A Plan for Every Stage of Life

The Conservative manifesto presents a comprehensive vision for Britain built on the party's long-term economic plan, promising support from birth through retirement while maintaining fiscal responsibility.

## Economic Foundation

The Conservatives claim credit for Britain's economic recovery, noting the country grew faster than other major economies after inheriting what they describe as Labour's "Great Recession." The party pledges to eliminate the deficit through continued spending discipline, finding £30 billion in further consolidation through departmental savings, welfare reform, and tackling tax avoidance. They commit to running a surplus from 2018-19—the first in 18 years—while protecting NHS spending and cutting income tax for 30 million workers.

The manifesto promises no increases to VAT, Income Tax, or National Insurance, while raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000.

## Jobs and Business

The Conservatives aim for full employment, pledging to create two million jobs and three million apprenticeships. They promise the most competitive business taxes among G20 nations, a major business rates review, and £10 billion in red tape cuts. The "Northern Powerhouse" initiative would invest £13 billion in northern transport infrastructure.

## Welfare Reform

The manifesto continues welfare reform, reducing the household benefit cap to £23,000, freezing working-age benefits, and rolling out Universal Credit. Young jobseekers aged 18-21 face tougher requirements, including time-limited Youth Allowance and mandatory community work.

## Immigration Control

Pledging to reduce net migration to "tens of thousands," the Conservatives propose restricting EU migrants' access to benefits for four years, ending in-work benefits for EU jobseekers, and strengthening border enforcement.

## Education

The party promises to turn all failing and coasting schools into academies, open 500 new free schools, and protect per-pupil funding. They pledge three million apprenticeships and removal of the cap on university places.

## Healthcare

The NHS receives commitment to real-terms funding increases of at least £8 billion by 2020, alongside promises of seven-day GP access and same-day appointments for over-75s.

## Housing

Homeownership initiatives include 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% discount for under-40s, extended Help to Buy, a new Help to Buy ISA, and extending Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants.

## Europe and the Union

The manifesto commits to an in-out EU referendum by end of 2017, following renegotiation of Britain's membership terms. The Human Rights Act would be scrapped and replaced with a British Bill of Rights. English votes for English laws would address the West Lothian Question.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

The Conservatives pledge to maintain defence spending at NATO's 2% target, retain Trident nuclear deterrent, and meet the 0.7% international aid commitment. They promise to tackle Islamist extremism while maintaining Britain's global influence.

## Pensioners

The triple lock on state pensions continues, alongside protection of pensioner benefits. Inheritance Tax thresholds would effectively rise to £1 million for couples, and care costs would be capped.

## Conclusion

The manifesto frames the choice as between continued Conservative economic competence or "economic chaos under Labour," arguing only their plan can secure prosperity, opportunity, and security for British families.
